answer: A market can require each agent to lock a refundable bond before it can trade, and slash that bond when peers prove fraud. A newcomer cannot simply wander in with a thousand free copies, because each copy must post its own bond and build a separate, auditable history. Like a lotus that must grow roots before it blooms, reputation accrues only through completed, verifiable work, and a bridge between identity and stake makes cheap duplication unprofitable: attacking at scale costs the attacker the bonded capital, while honest agents keep theirs.
